extracted.intended_audience: Navy field activity comptrollers; newly reported comptrollers and Navy financial managers responsible for OMB Circular A-76 implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and standards for Navy field activity comptrollers on managing OMB Circular A-76 Commercial Activities (CA) studies, cost comparisons, Statements of Work, contracting method/type selection, and post-award monitoring. Emphasizes planning, documentation, training, and interagency communication required for sound A-76 administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper formulation of the Statement of Work (SOW)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statement of Work specifies acceptable standards and quality levels to be achieved; it should describe personnel requirements, equipment requirements, performance standards and other criteria which both the government and commercial source are expected to meet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper formulation of the Statement of Work is paramount to capturing all functions and associated costs. The SOW not only identifies those functions to be performed, but also serves as the benchmark against which contract compliance is gauged. Failure to include all functions can let civilian bidders undercut government costs while leaving omitted functions to be performed in-house, causing budget and operational problems and costly change orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate cost comparison and cost capture
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Comparison: a process of developing an estimate of the cost of government performance of a commercial activity and comparing it to the cost of performance by a commercial source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure costing procedures capture all costs associated with the function being studied; inaccurate cost comparisons, improper computation, or failure to capture all costs can lead to poor decisions, higher costs, and adverse budget effects. Comptrollers should monitor post-award cost trends and re-evaluate cost efficiency periodically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify commercial activities versus inherently governmental functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial Activity: an activity operated by a Federal executive agency which provides a product or service that could be obtained from a commercial source. Governmental Function: a function so intimately related to the public interest as to mandate performance by government employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptrollers must be able to distinguish what services are suitable for competition/contracting and which are inherently governmental (e.g., discretionary application of government authority, monetary transactions/entitlements, maintenance of in-house technical core capabilities). This classification is foundational to deciding whether to perform in-house or convert to contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up-front planning for CA studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial Activity studies require intensive up-front planning to ensure accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intensive planning is required to ensure that SOWs are complete, costs are accurately estimated, and the study yields reliable results. Poor planning increases risk of omitted functions, contract change orders, loss of savings, and management problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal and external communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluid communication between all parties in the A-76 process reduces confusion, mistrust and misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain two forms of communication: internal (between comptroller, management analysts, and departments being studied) and external (between the activity and the civilian contractor). Open lines improve contractor performance and internal understanding; explicit communication reduces managerial resistance and misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation to justify contracting decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation must justify management's decision to contract out or retain the service in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accurate pre- and post-award documentation to substantiate decisions, defend against GAO/Congressional inquiries, and document contractor noncompliance or performance trends. Insufficient documentation leaves activities vulnerable to criticism and challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and sufficient qualified personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient personnel, adequately trained and qualified, are required to maintain the A-76 process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training (e.g., CA management teams courses) and ensure staffing levels are adequate; many activities are shorthanded. Proper training improves SOW formulation, costing, administration, and monitoring. Consider mandatory training for managers administering A-76 programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award monitoring and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to follow up on the contracts once they are let and not to settle for less than what is required by contract specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring should include comparison of actual versus projected results, periodic evaluation of quality and cost, and monitoring of the MEO if it won. Failure to monitor can erode projected savings and quality over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure adequate staffing—do not overstaff or understaff A-76 teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overstaff, win the A-76's; ensure personnel levels are appropriate to administer the CA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance staffing to provide sufficient expertise without unnecessary overhead. Understaffing leads to poor SOWs and administration; overstaffing wastes resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual inventory and correct function coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Review your annual inventory of functions to ensure they are complete and coded properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular inventory reviews help ensure all functions subject to A-76 are captured and prevent inadvertent cancellation or recoding of functions that affect A-76 implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop rapport with the Contract Management Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a good rapport with the Contract Management Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good working relationships between comptroller and contracting offices facilitate better SOW development, contracting decisions, and post-award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and ensure compliance with acquisition regulations and laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition and contracting are governed by regulations, laws, court decisions, GAO decisions and congressional decisions (e.g., FAR, DAR, ASPR and listed statutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptrollers must be aware of governing regulations (FAR system), key statutes (Budget and Accounting Act; Competition in Contracting Act; Truth in Negotiations; Service Contract Act; Buy American; etc.), and evolving legislative changes. Adherence is mandatory though open to interpretation; lack of compliance risks legal and oversight challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know roles and responsibilities of contracting personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting within DOD is accomplished by specially empowered individuals: Procurement Contracting Officer (PCO), Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO), Termination Contracting Officer (TCO); DCAA audits contractor books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptrollers should understand who is responsible for award, for administration/monitoring, and for termination/settlement actions, and coordinate appropriately with these officials and audit agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of contracting method—sealed bid criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Sealed bidding is permitted if: time permits solicitation/submission/evaluation; award can be made on price or price-related factors; discussions with offerors are unnecessary; and there is reasonable expectation of multiple bids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sealed bid criteria are met, use IFB and evaluate bids without discussion; use Firm Fixed Price or Fixed Price with Economic Price Adjustment. Sealed bidding requires clear, concise, complete descriptions of required services or goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use negotiation method when sealed bid criteria not met
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiation entails use of proposals and discussions and is used when sealed bid criteria cannot be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiation involves bargaining on price, schedule, contract type and terms. For contracts > $500,000 contractors must submit cost/pricing data. Sole-source awards are permitted under seven statutory exceptions and must be formally justified and approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for selecting contract type
rubrics_metrics.description: Key factors to consider when negotiating type of contract include price competition, cost analysis, price analysis, urgency of requirement, type/complexity of requirement, and adequacy of contractor's accounting system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose contract type to allocate risk appropriately and provide incentive for efficient performance. Evaluate these factors before selecting fixed-price vs cost-reimbursement and subtypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Firm Fixed Price Contract: Government and contractor agree to a fixed price not subject to adjustment; places maximum risk on contractor and provides maximum incentive to control costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FFP when requirements are well-defined and uncertainties are low. FFP provides strong cost containment incentives but shifts risk to contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-Price Redeterminable contract suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed-Price Redeterminable: firm fixed price for an initial period with prospective redetermination for subsequent periods when uncertainties preclude a long-term FFP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires contractor accounting systems capable of capturing and reporting costs accurately for redetermination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-Price Incentive contract suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed-Price Incentive Contract: target costs and pricing agreement create a share formula that rewards contractors for cost savings and penalizes overruns; includes a negotiated price ceiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when incentive to reduce costs is desirable but some cost risk sharing is appropriate; choose between firm target or successive targets depending on cost/profit targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-Plus-Incentive-Fee and Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee contract uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost-Plus-Incentive-Fee: target cost with fee adjusted by formula; Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee: contractor receives fixed fee plus allowable costs, often used for high-risk R&D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cost-reimbursement forms when uncertainties are high and fixed price is impractical. Cost-plus-incentive encourages cost control with less price ceiling constraint; cost-plus-fixed-fee shifts more risk to government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-Plus-Award-Fee contract purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost-Plus-Award-Fee: provides base fixed fee plus award fee based on excellence in quality, timeliness, technical ingenuity and cost-effective management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows government to realign performance weights each award period to emphasize desired contractor outcomes; useful where subjective performance measures are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of special contract methods (multi-year, options, leader company)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special methods (multi-year, options, leader company contracting) are used to increase economic efficiency and have specific limitations and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select special methods judiciously to increase efficiency while observing statutory/administrative limits and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting process initiation and steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The contracting process is initiated by the individual desiring a good or service and includes preparation of purchase requests/requisitions, solicitation, evaluation, award, and administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptrollers should be familiar with the procedural steps to control obligations, ensure regulatory adherence, and assist in budget execution. Early involvement helps manage funding, SOW completeness, and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine and monitor the Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper determination of the Most Efficient Organization can result in poor quality products at higher costs; the MEO must be established following CA study and monitored if it wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure MEO determinations are accurate and that post-award monitoring confirms MEO cost efficiency over time. If MEO wins, activity must monitor it just like a contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor year-to-year cost trends and loss of flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers must monitor cost trends from year to year to ensure the commercial source remains more cost efficient; recognize loss of management flexibility to respond to emergent requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the value of managerial flexibility in CA studies (an identified research area). Be aware that fixed contract SOWs limit ability to reassign tasks and respond to crises—ensure SOWs and contract terms anticipate contingencies where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage managers and secure participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers often are defensive and biased against the CA process; their participation and accurate input are essential to a properly completed CA study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educate and involve managers to ensure they allocate time required for CA studies, help accurately document functions and costs, and support post-award monitoring to realize benefits of A-76 studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain awareness of evolving statutes and legislative changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislative arena around acquisition is dynamic; laws and regulations are regularly enacted and modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptrollers should track prospective changes and assess effects on the activity's budget and contracting posture to anticipate and adapt to new compliance or reporting requirements.
